justifications.durability: The change is durable: the netCDF backend is declared in packages/imas-alambic/pyproject.toml (survives a clean reinstall), the py312 pin lives in the root pyproject's [tool.ruff.per-file-target-version], and the parse backstop test is committed. I built the wheel at head (imas_alambic-0.1.dev5869+gec3f7fbbd) and its METADATA declares Requires-Dist: imas-python[netcdf]>=2.3.0 -- the extra is in the artifact, not merely in the source. Deduction: the reviewed run's gate logs carry the header revision 177c82d8 (the base) while the tree held the uncommitted change, so the recorded revision names the checkout rather than the content measured; I re-ran the two gates at the reviewed head (ec3f7fbb) myself and both pass, which closes that provenance gap; the reviewed run's own uv.lock regeneration needed a scratch symlink workaround (documented in its evidence_inputs) because the dispatcher does not provision the sibling checkouts -- a one-off, not a defect. The three pre-existing drifts remain, so the plan's literal format clause is not durably closed.
justifications.evidence: Every quantitative claim I could reach was reproduced independently on this allocation. Wheel metadata at head declares imas-python[netcdf]; a fresh uv venv --python 3.12 dry-run of imas-python[netcdf]>=2.3.0 installs netcdf4==1.7.4 (matching the node's runtime figure); ruff check imas_ambix tests packages exits 0; pytest tests/test_serving_interpreter_parse.py -v reports 2 passed, 0 skipped with the engine-module discovery assertion holding. The negative control is falsified end to end with a positive control: ruff check --stdin-filename on a reverted eddb.py copy reports invalid-syntax at eddb.py:143, the 3.12 ast.parse names line 143, and the real eddb.py parses OK under the same serving interpreter. The pin's necessity is shown too -- formatting a copy at --target-version py314 rewrites both parenthesised clauses (lines 143 and 159) while the in-tree file is pinned to py312, so the per-file-target-version entry is load-bearing, not decorative. Deduction: I proved the clean-venv write claim by construction (wheel metadata plus the extra resolving to netcdf4 in a fresh 3.12 env) rather than re-running the write with the nova-cocos wheel, which lives in another checkout; the remaining residual is the three target-independent format drifts, which I reproduced (exit 1, same three files) and confirmed are independent of the pin (flagged under both target versions).
justifications.fit: The change matches Section 11 point for point: the imas-alambic netcdf extra, the py312 ruff pin by pattern (packages/imas-alambic/**/*.py -> py312) with the lock entries, the parse-backstop extension, and the evidence fragment. The commit subjects are conventional with a mechanism body and no trailer; no AI attribution and no plan/sprint/version label appears in a path, symbol or comment. The surviving pyproject comment explains the PEP 758 mechanism and its two measured incidents as mechanism text, not as a ticket reference. The fragment is honest about the unmet clause.
